import pandas as pd

def main():
    # List all source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_97/test_0.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_97/test_1.csv",

        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_97/test_6.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_97/test_7.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_97/test_8.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_97/test_9.csv"
    ]

    # Read all source tables into a list of DataFrames
    dfs = []
    for file_path in source_files:
        df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
        # Ensure schema and types match target schema
        df = df[['admit', 'gre', 'gpa', 'prestige']].copy()
        df['admit'] = df['admit'].astype(int)
        df['gre'] = df['gre'].astype(int)
        df['gpa'] = df['gpa'].astype(float)
        df['prestige'] = df['prestige'].astype(int)
        dfs.append(df)

    # Concatenate all source DataFrames into one DataFrame
    combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # The target table schema is the same as source schema, so no further transformation needed
    # Just ensure the dtypes are correct (already done above)

    # Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_97/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    combined_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
